dtsmartr v0.4.0 - API Summary & Programmatic Usage

Source: DTSMARTR_API_SUMMARY.md

Version: 0.4.0
Date: 2026-07-12
Package: Interactive Virtualized Data Explorer Grid Widget

📦 Package Overview

dtsmartr provides an interactive, virtualized data explorer widget built on React and htmlwidgets. It offers high-performance data exploration with virtual scrolling, multi-column sorting, advanced filtering, and column analytics.

Key Technologies: - React (via reactR) - Apache Arrow (IPC serialization) - htmlwidgets (R-to-JavaScript bridge) - Virtual scrolling for large datasets

🆕 New Functions in v0.4.0

Summary of Public API

Function Purpose Export Status
dtsmartr() Main widget constructor ✅ Exported
dtsmartr_options() Configuration builder ✅ Exported
dtsmartr_launch() External browser launcher + file wizard ✅ Exported
save_dtsmartr() Export to standalone HTML ✅ Exported
dtsmart_lite() / dtsmartr_lite() Lightweight viewer (no analytics) ✅ Exported (aliased)
dtsmartrOutput() Shiny output binding ✅ Exported
renderDtsmartr() Shiny render function ✅ Exported

📖 Function Reference

1. dtsmartr() - Main Widget Constructor

Purpose: Create an interactive virtualized data grid widget.

Signature:

dtsmartr(
  data,
  width         = NULL,
  height        = NULL,
  elementId     = NULL,
  datasetName   = NULL,
  options       = dtsmartr_options(),
  skip_routing  = FALSE  # Internal - do not use
)

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description
data data.frame required Dataset to explore
width character/numeric NULL Widget width (e.g., "100%", 800)
height character/numeric NULL Widget height (e.g., "100vh", 600)
elementId character NULL CSS ID for widget container
datasetName character Auto-detected Name shown in toolbar and generated code
options list dtsmartr_options() Configuration options (see below)
skip_routing logical FALSE Internal flag - ignore

Behavior: - Auto-detects column types (numeric, character, factor, datetime) - Serializes data to Apache Arrow IPC format (Base64) - Extracts column labels from attributes (attr(col, "label")) - Auto-routing: Datasets > 50,000 rows automatically redirect to dtsmartr_launch() to prevent IDE freezing

Returns: htmlwidget object (class dtsmartr)

Example:

library(dtsmartr)

# Basic usage
dtsmartr(mtcars)

# With options
dtsmartr(
  iris,
  datasetName = "Iris Dataset",
  options = dtsmartr_options(
    hidden_columns = c("Species"),
    header_density = "minimal",
    theme = "dark"
  )
)

# Large dataset (auto-routes to external browser)
big_data <- data.frame(x = 1:100000, y = rnorm(100000))
dtsmartr(big_data)  # Automatically calls dtsmartr_launch()

2. dtsmartr_options() - Configuration Builder

Purpose: Generate validated configuration options for the widget.

Signature:

dtsmartr_options(
  advanced_filter = TRUE,
  show_labels     = TRUE,
  column_picker   = TRUE,
  allow_export    = TRUE,
  theme           = "auto",
  na_string       = "NA",
  hidden_columns  = NULL,
  header_summary  = TRUE,
  header_density  = "auto",
  row_density     = "standard"
)

Parameters:

Parameter Type Options Default Description
advanced_filter logical TRUE/FALSE TRUE Show Advanced Filter side panel
show_labels logical TRUE/FALSE TRUE Display column labels from attributes
column_picker logical TRUE/FALSE TRUE Show column visibility dropdown
allow_export logical TRUE/FALSE TRUE Show “Query Code” button (R/SQL)
theme character "auto", "light", "dark" "auto" UI color theme
na_string character Any string "NA" Placeholder for missing values
hidden_columns character vector Column names NULL Columns to hide on load
header_summary logical TRUE/FALSE TRUE Show Kaggle-style column summaries
header_density character "auto", "minimal", "detailed" "auto" Header compression mode
row_density character "standard", "compact", "comfortable" "standard" Row spacing mode

New in v0.4.0: - ✨ header_density - Three-mode responsive header compression - ✨ row_density - Adjustable row spacing

Returns: Named list of validated settings

Example:

# Minimal configuration (no analytics)
opts_minimal <- dtsmartr_options(
  advanced_filter = FALSE,
  allow_export    = FALSE,
  header_summary  = FALSE,
  header_density  = "minimal"
)

# Dark theme with hidden columns
opts_dark <- dtsmartr_options(
  theme          = "dark",
  hidden_columns = c("ID", "USUBJID"),
  na_string      = "—"
)

# Comfortable row spacing
opts_comfort <- dtsmartr_options(
  row_density = "comfortable"
)

# Use with dtsmartr()
dtsmartr(mtcars, options = opts_minimal)

3. dtsmartr_launch() - External Browser Launcher

Purpose: Launch widget in external browser with optional file upload wizard.

Signature:

dtsmartr_launch(
  data    = NULL,
  port    = NULL,
  options = dtsmartr_options()
)

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description
data data.frame NULL Dataset to explore, or NULL for wizard mode
port numeric Auto Port number for Shiny server
options list dtsmartr_options() Configuration options

Modes:

A. Direct Mode (data provided)

Launches a temporary Shiny server and opens the dataset in the browser.

Use cases: - Large datasets (> 50,000 rows) - Avoiding IDE Viewer pane limitations - Full-screen exploration - Bypassing CORS restrictions

Example:

# Launch mtcars in browser
dtsmartr_launch(mtcars)

# Launch with dark theme
dtsmartr_launch(
  iris,
  options = dtsmartr_options(theme = "dark")
)

B. Wizard Mode (data = NULL)

Launches a zero-code file ingestion wizard powered by datamods.

Supported formats: - CSV (comma/semicolon/tab separated) - Excel (.xlsx, .xls) - SAS (.sas7bdat) - RDS (.rds)

Example:

# Launch file upload wizard
dtsmartr_launch()

# User can:
# 1. Upload CSV/Excel/SAS/RDS files
# 2. Preview data
# 3. Modify column types
# 4. Explore in interactive grid

Returns: No return value (called for side effect)

4. save_dtsmartr() - Export to Standalone HTML

Purpose: Export a dataset as a fully interactive, portable HTML file.

Signature:

save_dtsmartr(
  data,
  file,
  selfcontained = TRUE,
  title         = "dtsmartr",
  open          = FALSE,
  background    = "white",
  libdir        = NULL,
  width         = NULL,
  height        = NULL,
  elementId     = NULL,
  options       = dtsmartr_options(),
  verbose       = TRUE
)

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description
data data.frame required Dataset to export
file character required Output file path (.html auto-appended)
selfcontained logical TRUE Embed all assets in single file
title character "dtsmartr" Browser tab title
open logical FALSE Open in browser after saving
background character "white" Page background color
libdir character NULL Library folder path (if selfcontained = FALSE)
width numeric NULL Widget width in pixels
height numeric NULL Widget height in pixels
elementId character NULL CSS ID for widget
options list dtsmartr_options() Configuration options
verbose logical TRUE Print confirmation message

Output Modes:

selfcontained Output Size Best For
TRUE (default) Single .html file Larger Email, sharing
FALSE .html + _files/ folder Smaller Local use, large datasets

Returns: Absolute path to saved file (invisibly)

Example:

# Basic export (single file)
save_dtsmartr(mtcars, "mtcars_report.html")

# Open in browser immediately
save_dtsmartr(iris, "iris.html", open = TRUE)

# Non-self-contained (for large datasets)
save_dtsmartr(
  big_data,
  "big_report.html",
  selfcontained = FALSE,
  title = "Big Data Analysis"
)

# With custom options
save_dtsmartr(
  mtcars,
  "mtcars_dark.html",
  options = dtsmartr_options(
    theme = "dark",
    header_density = "minimal"
  ),
  background = "#1a202c",
  open = TRUE
)

File Size Considerations: - React runtime: ~120 KB (gzipped) - Data: Proportional to dataset size - For datasets > 100k rows: use selfcontained = FALSE

5. dtsmart_lite() / dtsmartr_lite() - Lightweight Viewer

Purpose: Simplified data viewer with analytics features disabled.

Signature:

dtsmart_lite(data, title = NULL, ...)
dtsmartr_lite(data, title = NULL, ...)  # Alias

Parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description
data data.frame required Dataset to view
title character NULL Dataset name
... Additional arguments — Passed to dtsmartr()

Automatically disables: - ❌ Advanced Filter panel - ❌ Query Code export button - ❌ Column summary statistics (histograms, bars)

Enabled features: - ✅ Basic filtering (per-column) - ✅ Sorting (click headers) - ✅ Column visibility toggle - ✅ Virtual scrolling

Use cases: - Quick data preview - Sharing with non-technical users - Reducing visual clutter - Faster rendering (no summary calculations)

Example:

# Quick preview
dtsmart_lite(mtcars)

# With custom title
dtsmart_lite(iris, title = "Iris Flowers")

# Still accepts additional arguments
dtsmart_lite(
  mtcars,
  title = "Motor Trends",
  width = "100%",
  height = "600px"
)

Equivalent to:

dtsmartr(
  data,
  datasetName = title,
  options = dtsmartr_options(
    advanced_filter = FALSE,
    allow_export    = FALSE,
    header_summary  = FALSE
  )
)

6. Shiny Bindings

dtsmartrOutput() - Shiny Output Binding

Purpose: Create a dtsmartr output element in Shiny UI.

Signature:

dtsmartrOutput(outputId, width = '100%', height = '400px')

Example:

library(shiny)
library(dtsmartr)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("dtsmartr in Shiny"),
  dtsmartrOutput("grid", width = "100%", height = "600px")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$grid <- renderDtsmartr({
    dtsmartr(mtcars)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

renderDtsmartr() - Shiny Render Function

Purpose: Render a dtsmartr widget inside Shiny server.

Signature:

renderDtsmartr(expr, env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE)

Example:

# Reactive dataset
server <- function(input, output) {
  data <- reactive({
    mtcars[mtcars$cyl == input$cyl_filter, ]
  })
  
  output$grid <- renderDtsmartr({
    dtsmartr(
      data(),
      options = dtsmartr_options(theme = input$theme)
    )
  })
}

🎯 Programmatic Usage Patterns

Pattern 1: Basic Exploration

library(dtsmartr)

# Load and explore
dtsmartr(mtcars)

# With pharmaverse CDISC data
library(pharmaverseadam)
dtsmartr(adsl)

Pattern 2: Customized Views

# Dark theme with minimal headers
dtsmartr(
  iris,
  options = dtsmartr_options(
    theme          = "dark",
    header_density = "minimal",
    row_density    = "compact"
  )
)

# Hide sensitive columns
dtsmartr(
  patient_data,
  options = dtsmartr_options(
    hidden_columns = c("SSN", "MRN", "DOB")
  )
)

Pattern 3: Batch HTML Export

# Export multiple datasets
datasets <- list(
  mtcars = mtcars,
  iris   = iris,
  airquality = airquality
)

for (name in names(datasets)) {
  save_dtsmartr(
    datasets[[name]],
    file = paste0("reports/", name, "_report.html"),
    title = paste(name, "Report"),
    options = dtsmartr_options(theme = "light")
  )
}

Pattern 4: Shiny Dashboard

library(shiny)
library(dtsmartr)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Data Explorer"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("dataset", "Choose Dataset:",
                  choices = c("mtcars", "iris", "airquality")),
      selectInput("theme", "Theme:",
                  choices = c("auto", "light", "dark")),
      selectInput("density", "Header Density:",
                  choices = c("auto", "minimal", "detailed"))
    ),
    mainPanel(
      dtsmartrOutput("grid", height = "700px")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  data <- reactive({
    get(input$dataset)
  })
  
  output$grid <- renderDtsmartr({
    dtsmartr(
      data(),
      datasetName = input$dataset,
      options = dtsmartr_options(
        theme = input$theme,
        header_density = input$density
      )
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Pattern 5: Conditional Routing

# Automatic routing based on size
explore_data <- function(df) {
  if (nrow(df) > 50000) {
    message("Large dataset detected - launching in browser")
    dtsmartr_launch(df)
  } else {
    dtsmartr(df)
  }
}

# Use it
explore_data(small_df)   # Opens in Viewer pane
explore_data(large_df)   # Opens in browser

Pattern 6: Report Generation

# Generate interactive report
generate_report <- function(data, output_file, title) {
  save_dtsmartr(
    data,
    file = output_file,
    title = title,
    selfcontained = TRUE,
    open = TRUE,
    options = dtsmartr_options(
      header_density = "auto",
      theme = "auto",
      allow_export = TRUE
    ),
    background = "white"
  )
}

# Create report
generate_report(
  mtcars,
  "mtcars_analysis.html",
  "Motor Trends Analysis 2024"
)

📊 Data Type Handling

Automatically detected types:

R Type JavaScript Type Display
logical logical TRUE/FALSE
integer integer Whole numbers
numeric numeric Decimals
character character Text
factor factor Categorical (converted to character)
Date datetime Date strings
POSIXct / POSIXlt datetime DateTime strings

Conversions on serialization: - Factors → characters - Dates → ISO strings - POSIXt → ISO strings

🚀 Performance Characteristics

Dataset Size Recommended Method Rendering
< 10k rows dtsmartr() Viewer pane
10k - 50k rows dtsmartr() Viewer pane
> 50k rows dtsmartr_launch() External browser (auto)
> 100k rows save_dtsmartr(selfcontained=FALSE) Static HTML

Virtual scrolling: Only visible rows are rendered, enabling smooth performance on datasets with millions of rows.

📦 Dependencies

Core: - arrow - Data serialization (Apache Arrow IPC) - base64enc - Base64 encoding - htmlwidgets - R-to-JavaScript bridge - reactR - React integration - jsonlite - JSON serialization

UI: - shiny - Server functionality - datamods - File upload wizard - htmltools - HTML generation

Optional: - bslib - Bootstrap themes (for wizard mode)

🎨 UI Features Summary (v0.4.0)

Original Features (v0.4.0)

  1. ✅ Compact Header Mode - Responsive density controls (Min/Auto/Detail)
  2. ✅ Advanced Filter Side Panel - Multi-condition query builder with live preview
  3. ✅ Shift+Click Multi-Column Sorting - Excel-style multi-sort with numbered badges

UI Enhancements (v0.4.0)

  1. ✅ Smart Sparkline Hiding - Constant/binary/low-variance columns show specialized summaries
  2. ✅ Direct Click-to-Sort - Full column header clickable (larger target)
  3. ✅ Binary Column Visualization - Split bars for yes/no columns
  4. ✅ Low Cardinality Display - Category pills for columns with < 5 unique values
  5. ✅ Enhanced Drag-Drop - Glow effect during column reordering
  6. ✅ Layout Stability - Fixed button collapse in compact mode

📝 Migration Guide

From v0.3.0 to v0.4.0

New Parameters: - header_density in dtsmartr_options() - row_density in dtsmartr_options()

Behavioral Changes: - Datasets > 50k rows auto-route to dtsmartr_launch() (bypass with skip_routing = TRUE internally) - Filter keyboard shortcut changed: Ctrl+Shift+F → Ctrl+Alt+F (browser compatibility)

No Breaking Changes: All v0.3.0 code remains compatible.

🐛 Troubleshooting

Issue: Large dataset freezes IDE

Solution: Use dtsmartr_launch() or save_dtsmartr()

Issue: Missing column labels

Solution: Ensure columns have label attribute:

attr(df$my_column, "label") <- "My Column Label"

Issue: Widget not rendering in Shiny

Solution: Check height is specified:

dtsmartrOutput("grid", height = "600px")

Issue: Selfcontained HTML too large

Solution: Use selfcontained = FALSE:

save_dtsmartr(df, "report.html", selfcontained = FALSE)
